finding_list.consequence: When Stripe throws (declined card, network error, bad customer), charge() logs and returns undefined. checkout.js treats a falsy payment as not failed and marks the order paid with a null payment_intent_id, returning 201, so goods are ordered without payment.

The password UPDATE is fired without await. If it fails, the rejection is unhandled (can crash the Node process or be silently lost), while the handler still deletes other sessions and returns { ok: true }, so the user believes the password changed when it did not. The session DELETE can also race ahead of the update.
Any signed-in user can read any other customer's order, including shipping address and items, by requesting /orders/<id> (insecure direct object reference).

When Stripe throws (declined card, network error, bad customer), charge() logs and returns undefined. checkout.js treats a falsy payment as success: the order is marked paid with a null payment_intent_id and the customer gets 201, so goods ship without payment and the order cannot be refunded.

Under default READ COMMITTED isolation, two concurrent checkouts can both read the same times_used below max_uses, both pass, and both write times_used + 1, so a limited coupon is redeemed more times than allowed and the counter under-counts.
The unauthenticated search endpoint concatenates q and category into SQL, so an attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, reading or modifying any table (users, session tokens, orders).
